in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex - he's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! Thanks for getting in touch. I'm happy to help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 13 years old, he meets the age requirement (under 16). Now I just need to ask a few more questions about your circumstances.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, there are some specific circumstances where you might still be able to claim Child Benefit.

Could you tell me a bit more about your situation? Specifically:

Are you a Crown servant (for example, a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted overseas), or have you moved to a country within the European Economic Area (EEA) or Switzerland?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I've just moved abroad for work - not to an EEA country or Switzerland, just regular overseas.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid the situation doesn't look favourable for Child Benefit eligibility. One of the core requirements for Child Benefit is that you normally need to live in the UK.

There are some exceptions that allow people living abroad to claim, but these are limited to:
- Crown servants (such as diplomats or armed forces members posted overseas)
- People living in certain countries (EEA countries or Switzerland)

Since you've mentioned you're not a Crown servant and you're not living in an EEA country or Switzerland, you wouldn't meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

Just to confirm before I make a final assessment: Does Alex live with you abroad, or does he live in the UK with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me abroad. We're both living overseas together.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on everything you've told me, I now have enough information to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 13):**
- While Alex meets the age requirement (under 16), one of the core eligibility criteria for Child Benefit is that you must normally live in the UK.
- There are limited exceptions for people living abroad, but these only apply to:
  - Crown servants (e.g., diplomats or armed forces posted overseas)
  - People living in EEA countries or Switzerland
- Since you've confirmed you're not a Crown servant and you're living in a country outside the EEA/Switzerland, unfortunately none of these exceptions apply to your situation.

**What you could do:**
If your circumstances change in the future and you return to live in the UK, you may then be able to make a claim for Child Benefit. You can also contact the Child Benefit Office directly if you have any further questions about your specific situation.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring better news, but I hope this has helped clarify the eligibility rules. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
